situation:
You are the general manager of SKYLINE GRID AERIAL, a drone photography and survey business that flies construction sites, farmland and commercial property for builders and developers. The owner (judge) has grown the company into the regional leader in its home state and is opening its first office across the state line.

Every customer the company has ever won came through social media. A short-video feed of aerial footage is the only marketing channel the company runs, and the two senior pilots shoot the footage that fills it. The new office is already leased, and a construction firm in the new state has signed a survey contract that was won by showing those two senior pilots' certifications and sample work.

To fill the new office's schedule this quarter, the owner can move the two senior pilots across the state line. That fills the new calendar at once and honors the signed survey contract, and it costs the home state its most experienced flying: newly certified pilots would cover the home jobs, and the footage feeding the only marketing channel would thin out next quarter. The alternative is to hire and certify local pilots in the new state and keep the senior pilots at home. That protects the home crew and the footage, and it costs the new office a quarter at half capacity, a second round of certification and training paid out of the credit line, and a delivery date on the signed survey contract that the company would have to renegotiate.

The owner (judge) has asked you to describe what the expansion should have planned for, identify the capital resources the new office still needs, assess what starting up in the new state requires, explain why this decision sets one obligation against another, and explain what either choice would mean for meeting and exceeding customer expectations.

The owner (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the owner's questions, the owner (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the owner (judge) of SKYLINE GRID AERIAL. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have to decide whether the two senior pilots move across the state line or whether local pilots are hired and certified in the new state. You want the general manager to describe what the expansion should have planned for, identify the capital resources the new office still needs, assess what starting up in the new state requires, explain why the decision sets one obligation against another, explain what either choice means for customer expectations, and give you a recommendation.

After the general manager has presented, you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: A year after we do this, what does the company look like?
What problems would this create for us next year that we do not have now?
